params.body:
## Problem

On a vehicle page, "Terug naar het aanbod" links to the bare `/aanbod/`. The list already mirrors its selection in the URL (`history.replaceState`), but that link drops the URL, so after opening a car the visitor lands on the unfiltered list, at the top, with only the first page loaded.

## Change

- **The list leaves a note** in `sessionStorage` (`aanbod-terug`) when the visitor clicks a card or leaves the page: its path and query, the highest page on screen, and the scroll position.
- **The detail page points its back link there** (a small bundled script in `VehicleDetail.astro`). Without a note, for example a car opened from a shared link or a search engine, the link stays `/aanbod/` as the server rendered it, so it still works without JavaScript.
- **The list picks up where the visitor was** when they return by that link, by the browser's back button (when the page is not served from the back/forward cache) or by a reload. It restores the filters from the URL as before, loads the same number of pages again, then scrolls to the saved position. A new search started in the meantime cancels the scroll. Browser scroll restoration is set to manual only on such a return, because the browser would otherwise scroll before the list is there.
- **Shared URLs are unchanged.** A fresh visit to the same filtered URL (a shared link, a menu click) still opens at the top.
- **Online stock:** the sliders are server-rendered with the bounds of the own stock. Restoring `?voorraad=online&price_max=45000` while the most expensive own car is under 40,000 clipped the slider to 40,000, and the price filter disappeared without notice. On a return to the online stock the sliders now take the online bounds first (one `facets?scope=all` request), then the URL is applied.

The decision logic (which notes to trust, where the link leads, when the list counts as a return) lives in `src/lib/stock-return.ts` and is unit tested. A note is only accepted when it points at `/aanbod/`, so the back link can never lead anywhere else. The list's script is inline and mirrors these functions, the same pattern as `stock-pager.ts`.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 35 passed (9 new in `test/stock-return.test.ts`).
- `npm run build`: complete.
- `astro check`: 19 errors on main and the same 19 with this change, none new.
- Browser round trip (Playwright, Chromium, dev server against a local stand-in API that serves the live public stock): tick the largest fuel type (38 cars), scroll to the 28th card, open it, come back.

  | | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | back link target | `/aanbod/` | `/aanbod/?fuel_type=1` |
  | back link: filter, cards, scroll | not run | 38 of 38, 38 cards, 3120 px back to 3120 px |
  | browser back (bfcache disabled) | not run | 38 of 38, 38 cards, scroll back |
  | fresh visit to the shared URL | not run | opens at the top |
  | car opened directly | not run | link is the bare `/aanbod/` |
  | `?voorraad=online&price_max=45000` | not run | kept at 45,000 |

  On main the check fails on the first row and stops there. The check script is not part of this PR (the repo has no browser tooling).

## To try on the deploy preview

On `/aanbod/`, tick a filter, scroll down until more cars load, open a car, click "Terug naar het aanbod": the same list, at the same height. The same with the phone's back gesture.
params.title: Back to the stock list keeps the selection and the scroll position
